# A popped-out vessel docks back into main when the pointer enters it

## Context

This surfaced while I was clearing the one Brain-gated red on `#19840`. On a hosted runner, `WorkstationPopOutHoverSyncNL.spec.mjs:90` failed both attempts with `page.evaluate: Target page, context or browser has been closed`: the popup closed under the test about 2.4 s after it connected. The spec passes on dev's runs and locally because it finishes in about 1.3 s. Six arms in `BRAIN_QUARANTINES` (`buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs`) are marked "hosted only" or "hosted, intermittent". One of them, `WorkstationPopOutSparklinesNL`, names the same symptom: "the popup closes while a sparkline cell is being captured".

**Observed.** Setup: headless `chrome` channel, local, Engine dev `44534e3128`, Brain dev `afae1ef3`. I used an untracked probe copy of the HoverSync arm that holds the popup open instead of closing it.
- **Pointer moved into the popup:** 10 of 10 runs closed it. The popup's `window.close()` ran about 2.0 s after the pop-out click unthrottled (6 runs) and about 3 s at 4× CPU throttle (4 runs).
  - Main-thread stack: `Main.windowNativeClose` ← `RemoteMethodAccess.onRemoteMethod`.
  - App Worker stack, from a hot-patched `NativeLifecycle#retire`: `Workspace.retireReturnedVessel` ← `Workspace.commitCrossWindowTransfer` ← `DragCoordinator.commitNativeWindowDrop`.
  - Receipt: `lastTearOutClose {itemId: 'feed', stage: 'acknowledged', dispatch: 'native', closed: true}`. A wrapped `TearOut#retireVessel` was never called.
- **No pointer in the popup:** 2 of 2 runs kept it open for 4 s, and nothing retired.
- **The popup never moved.** From its first sample until the close, its own `screenX`/`screenY` read (34, 749) at 1576×240. Main sits at (22, 22), 1600×900, so the vessel opens over main where the pane was.

**Inference:** the engine committed a native-titlebar drop that nobody performed.

## The Problem

The vessel's first `pointermove` is not a move, but it publishes geometry:
1. `WindowPosition#armViewportProbe` takes one pointer sample to measure where the viewport starts inside the frame.
2. `neoViewportOffset` starts unset, so that first sample calls `publishGeometry()`.
3. The publication carries no `nativeEffect`.

`DragCoordinator#onWindowPositionChange` reads any untagged publication from a vessel the workspace owns as a title-bar move:
1. `defaultResolveNativeWindowDrag` resolves the vessel as a drag source on ownership alone.
2. The candidate finds main's dock under the vessel, because the vessel opened at the pane's own rect.
3. Dwell (1200 ms), settle (250 ms) and handoff (180 ms) run out.
4. `commitNativeWindowDrop` returns the pane to main and closes the vessel.

So a pane popped out with the header action docks back into main about 1.6 s after the pointer first enters its window. The e2e tier reads this as hosted flake, because an arm passes whenever it finishes inside that window. The behavior is witnessed headless. Headed should behave the same by construction (same probe, same coordinator, and the vessel opens over main by design), but nobody has witnessed it headed yet.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/main/addon/WindowPosition.mjs`:
  - `armViewportProbe` takes one `pointermove` sample into `win.neoViewportOffset`, then calls `publishGeometry()` when the offset is new.
  - `onResize` publishes a fixed-origin resize the same way.
- `src/worker/App.mjs` `onWindowPositionChange` passes one payload to `Neo.manager.Window`, then to `Neo.manager.DragCoordinator`.
- `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs`:
  - `onWindowPositionChange` returns early on `nativeEffect`. Otherwise it resolves a source through `getNativeWindowDragSource` and starts or re-arms a candidate.
  - The timers are `nativeWindowDropDwellMs: 1200`, `nativeWindowDropSettleMs: 250` and `nativeWindowDropHandoffMs: 180`, followed by `commitNativeWindowDrop`.
- `src/dashboard/dock/window/Participation.mjs` `defaultResolveNativeWindowDrag`: any owned vessel window is a drag source. Nothing asks whether the window moved.
- `apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs`: `commitCrossWindowTransfer` → `retireReturnedVessel` → `NativeLifecycle#retire` → `closeTearOutVessel` → `NativeVesselTransaction.closeVessel` → `Main.windowNativeClose`.

Design authority:
- `DragCoordinator#onWindowPositionChange`: "Consumes high-frequency window geometry updates for native OS-titlebar popup drags, where the browser does not emit pointer move/up events."
- `WindowPosition#publishGeometry`: "Advancing this baseline prevents the poll from echoing that same position as an untagged user move."
- ADR-0029's native title-bar path (#13028) is for a popup dragged by its title bar.

A publication that does not move the window is none of these.

Prior art: Mnemosyne's 2026-09-26 probes (Memory Core session `9f1b8628-238d-4ab9-b47e-9c08c5df5781`) saw CDP placements of a committed popup over main dock into main after the dwell, and read them as instrument artifacts. A CDP placement is a move. This case has no move at all.

## The Fix

In `DragCoordinator#onWindowPositionChange`, read a title-bar move as a change of the window's origin:
- Keep each window's last published origin (`screenLeft`/`screenTop`), including `nativeEffect` publications, so an engine move becomes the baseline.
- Start no native drop gesture from a publication that repeats that origin.
- A candidate that is already running keeps receiving publications as it does today.

The method's JSDoc states the rule. `WindowPosition` stays as it is, so the measured offset still reaches `Neo.manager.Window`.

Contract ledger: n/a. No config, signature or payload changes.
Decision Record impact: aligned-with ADR-0029 (the native title-bar path).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A unit arm in `test/playwright/unit/manager/DragCoordinator.spec.mjs`, red on dev: a vessel publication that repeats its last origin starts no native drop candidate, and one that moves the origin still does.
- [x] A whitebox e2e arm, red on dev, where the vessel closes through `commitNativeWindowDrop` at about 2 s. It pops out the Feed pane with the header action, moves the pointer into the vessel and holds past dwell + settle (≥ 3 s). Pass: the vessel is still open and still holds the pane.
- [x] The native title-bar witnesses stay green at the fix head: `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL`, `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL`.
- [x] The `WorkstationPopOutSparklinesNL` entry leaves `BRAIN_QUARANTINES`, with the receipt that ties its symptom ("the popup closes while a sparkline cell is being captured") to this mechanism. *(Narrowed 2026-10-17 from "each entry": the other five get their own hosted run, below.)*

Evidence per AC: PR #19842's AC table at the head the operator merged (`e7ac348959`, 2026-10-17). It was approved by Euclid (review 5560266267), and its checks passed at that head.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] *(operator's hand)* Pop out a pane in the Workstation, move the mouse into its window and wait 3 s: the pane stays popped out.
- [ ] The other five `BRAIN_QUARANTINES` entries run at the merged head, each lifted in its own burn-in under #19655. An entry whose arm then passes leaves the list. One that still fails keeps its row, with the finding that this mechanism does not explain it.

## Out of Scope

- Where the vessel opens. Lifting the pane at its own rect is the pop-out's design (`HeaderActions#measureDockPaneRect`).
- The dwell, settle and handoff timings.
- `WindowPosition`'s probe and its movement poll.

## Avoided Traps

- **Opening the vessel beside main:** this changes product placement and leaves the misread in place for any vessel over main.
- **Tagging only the probe's publication:** a fixed-origin resize (`onResize`) would still read as a drag.
- **A longer dwell, or quarantining HoverSync too:** both move the race and call a product bug flake.

* fix(dock): a native title-bar drop starts only when the window's origin moves (#19841)

A window publishes geometry for more than movement: its first sample, the
viewport offset its first pointer sample measures, a resize that keeps its
origin. DragCoordinator read every untagged publication from an owned vessel
as the OS dragging it, and a popped-out pane opens over main where it was, so
the first pointer move into it docked the pane back after the dwell.

The coordinator now records each window's last published origin (engine
moves included) and starts a native gesture only from a changed one; a
window's first publication only sets its baseline, and a running gesture
keeps every frame. The unit arms that published a stationary window as a
drag frame now model the move.
